dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Today we meet the luckiest hand in mahjong: 天糊 Heavenly Hand. The dealer looks at the fourteen tiles just dealt and the hand is already complete.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: So the dealer wins before anyone even discards?

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Exactly. No draws, no discards, no calls — just the dealt hand. It is a limit hand, so it counts as 10 faan.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: One trap: if the dealer declares a concealed kong first, the win is no longer 天糊. The hand no longer comes straight from the deal.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: Got it — the deal itself has to be the winning hand.

questions.question: Who is the only player who can win 天糊 Heavenly Hand?
options: The dealer
Any non-dealer who is waiting after the deal
The player to the dealer's right
Any player who has not discarded yet
questions.explanation: 天糊 belongs to the dealer: the fourteen tiles dealt at the start of the hand must already be a winning hand.

questions.question: When exactly does 天糊 happen?
options: On the dealt fourteen tiles, before any tile is discarded
On the dealer's first drawn tile after the deal
On the first discard the dealer makes
On the dealer's second turn
questions.explanation: No turn is played at all — the deal is the win, so nothing may be drawn, discarded or called first.

questions.question: How many faan is 天糊 worth?
questions.explanation: 天糊 is one of the limit hands, so it is always scored at the 10 faan ceiling.

questions.question: Which statements about 天糊 are correct?
options: Only the dealer can win it
It is won on the tiles dealt at the start of the hand
A declared concealed kong cancels it
A non-dealer can win it if their dealt hand is complete
questions.explanation: A complete dealt hand for a non-dealer is not 天糊 — 天糊 is the dealer's alone; the other three statements are true.

questions.question: Match each term to what it means for 天糊.

pairs.right: Dealer wins on the fourteen dealt tiles
Declaring one before the win cancels 天糊
The value of the hand however the tiles fell

questions.explanation: The deal supplies the win, so any action such as a kong means the hand is no longer the hand that was dealt.

questions.question: The dealer is dealt a complete hand but first declares a concealed kong, then wins on the replacement tile. What is the result?
options: Still 天糊, because the hand was dealt complete
Not 天糊; it is an ordinary win after the kong
The hand is void and must be thrown away
It becomes 地糊 instead
questions.explanation: Once the dealer declares a kong the win no longer comes straight from the dealt hand, so only the normal faan apply.

questions.question: The dealer is dealt thirteen tiles and is waiting only on {{p3}}. Which tile must the fourteenth dealt tile be for 天糊?
options: p3
p4
m3
east
questions.explanation: 天糊 needs the dealt hand to be complete, so the last dealt tile has to be the exact tile the thirteen tiles were waiting on.

questions.question: A player wins 天糊 by self-draw. How many points does each of the other three players pay?
questions.explanation: At 10 faan a self-draw pays 64 from each player, so the winner collects 192 in total.

13-8.title: Earthly Hand
13-8.subtitle: Winning on the dealer's first discard

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: 地糊 Earthly Hand is the non-dealer's version of that dream: thirteen dealt tiles that are already waiting.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: And then I just need the dealer's first discard?

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Exactly — the dealer's very first discard, before you call anything. It is a limit hand, 10 faan.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Two things kill it: the dealer declares a concealed kong first, or you call a meld before the win.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: Stay silent, stay dealt, and grab that first discard.

questions.question: Who can win 地糊 Earthly Hand?
options: A non-dealer whose dealt hand is already waiting
The dealer on the dealt tiles
Any player after the first discard
The player who discards first
questions.explanation: 地糊 is a non-dealer's hand: the thirteen dealt tiles must already be in tenpai, waiting for one tile.

questions.question: Which tile must complete a 地糊?
options: The dealer's very first discard
Any discard during the first rotation
A tile the player draws themselves
A tile taken from the wall after a kong
questions.explanation: The win comes from the dealer's first discard and nothing else — a later discard is just an ordinary win.

questions.question: How many faan is 地糊 worth?
questions.explanation: 地糊 is a limit hand, so it is scored at the 10 faan ceiling.

questions.question: Which of these are required for 地糊?
options: The winner is a non-dealer
The thirteen dealt tiles are already waiting
The winner calls no meld before the win
The winner may call a Chow before claiming the win
questions.explanation: Calling a meld would mean the hand is no longer the dealt hand, so 地糊 needs the thirteen dealt tiles untouched.

questions.question: Match each hand or situation to its result.

pairs.right: Dealer wins on the fourteen dealt tiles
Non-dealer wins on the dealer's first discard

pairs.left: Dealer's concealed kong before the first discard
pairs.right: 地糊 is no longer available

questions.explanation: Both hands come from the deal, but only 地糊 depends on the dealer's first discard staying the first discard.

questions.question: A non-dealer is dealt thirteen tiles waiting only on {{s7}}. Which tile must the dealer discard first for 地糊?
options: s7
s6
s8
p7
questions.explanation: The dealt hand is already waiting on one tile, and 地糊 needs that exact tile to be the dealer's first discard.

questions.question: The dealer declares a concealed kong, then makes the first discard. A waiting non-dealer claims it. What happens?
options: It is still 地糊
It is not 地糊; it is an ordinary discard win
The claim is illegal
It becomes 天糊
questions.explanation: The rules say the dealer's concealed kong cancels 地糊, because that discard no longer comes straight after the deal.

questions.question: A non-dealer wins 地糊 on the dealer's first discard. How many points does the dealer pay?
questions.explanation: 地糊 is 10 faan and it is a discard win, so the discarder — the dealer — pays the full 128 alone.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: 九蓮寶燈 Nine Gates looks like a straight line: 1112345678999 of one suit, plus one extra tile of that same suit.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: That is thirteen tiles already. So the base hand waits on every tile of the suit?

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Yes — all nine. That is why it is called nine gates, and it counts as 10 faan.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: The hand must be fully concealed. On a self-draw you simply win; on a discard you must be calling 九扉 nine gates.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: Same suit, no melds, and call 九扉 if someone else throws the tile.

questions.question: What is the shape of a 九蓮寶燈 Nine Gates hand?
options: 1112345678999 of one suit plus one more tile of the same suit
Four triplets and a pair of honours
Thirteen different terminals and honours
Two sequences of the same suit plus a pair
questions.explanation: The whole hand is one suit: the run of 1112345678999 with any single extra tile of that same suit.

questions.question: Which requirements must a 九蓮寶燈 hand meet?
options: All tiles come from one suit
The hand is fully concealed
The base pattern 1112345678999 is present plus one extra tile of that suit
At least one honour triplet is included
questions.explanation: Honours are impossible in Nine Gates — the hand is a single suit, held without any open meld.

questions.question: How many different tiles does the thirteen-tile Nine Gates base 1112345678999 wait on?
questions.explanation: Any tile from 1 to 9 of that suit completes the pattern, which is exactly where the name nine gates comes from.

questions.question: How many faan is 九蓮寶燈 worth?
questions.explanation: Nine Gates is a limit hand, so it is scored at the 10 faan ceiling rather than adding more faan on top.

questions.question: The winning tile is thrown by another player. What must the winner have called?
options: 九扉 nine gates
A concealed kong
Nothing — a discard win needs no call
An open Chow to prove the suit
questions.explanation: A discard win only counts if the player is calling nine gates (九扉); self-draw needs no such declaration.

questions.question: The player completes the 1112345678999 pattern plus the extra tile by self-draw. What else is required?
options: Nothing extra — the completed pattern wins
A 九扉 declaration first
An open meld to prove the suit
A kong of the extra tile
questions.explanation: On a self-draw, completing the pattern is enough — the 九扉 call matters only when the tile is discarded by someone else.

questions.question: A player's hand is built on {{m1}}{{m1}}{{m1}}{{m2}}{{m3}}{{m4}}{{m5}}{{m6}}{{m7}}{{m8}}{{m9}}{{m9}}{{m9}}. Which of these may be the extra fourteenth tile?
options: m5
p5
s5
east
questions.explanation: Nine Gates allows one suit only, so the extra tile must be a Character tile like the rest of the hand.

questions.question: Before winning, the player called a Chow to complete a run. Can the hand still be 九蓮寶燈?
options: Yes, if the tiles still form 1112345678999
No — the hand must be fully concealed
Yes, but only on a self-draw
Only if the Chow was in the same suit
questions.explanation: Nine Gates requires a fully concealed hand, so any open meld rules it out even if the tiles look right.
